title: NSAT General Mock Test 08

instructions: Marking scheme: +4 for correct, -1 for incorrect
Answer all questions - no optional sections

questions.questionText: A school organized a quiz competition where three students, Amit, Bina, and Chetan, participated. Each of them answered exactly 140 questions, but the total number of distinct questions answered by all three was only 200. A question is considered easy if it was answered by all three students and difficult if it was answered by only one of them. What is the difference between the number of difficult questions and the number of easy questions?

A bus from Delhi to Jaipur has six stoppages on its route (excluding Jaipur). After the bus leaves Delhi, four people, each with different tickets, board it. What is the maximum number of different sets of tickets they could have?

A man lent Rs 65,000 to his friends Aman and Shinu. He lent a part of the amount to Aman at 5% interest rate and the remaining amount to Shinu at 8% interest rate. At the end of the year, the interest earned from both was equal. What was the interest rate on the total amount?

Nathan owns a model airplane that he decides to sell to Liam. The model airplane costs Nathan $60, and he plans to sell it for $150. Between Nathan’s house and Liam’s house is a 6-mile-wide river. Liam’s house is located 28 miles downstream on the opposite side of the river. To deliver the model airplane, Nathan must cross the river using a boat and then drive the remaining distance in a car. The boat charges $0.6 per mile and travels at a speed of 12 miles per hour. The car charges $1.2 per mile and travels at a speed of 25 miles per hour. Liam requires Nathan to deliver the airplane by 7:00 p.m., and for every hour Nathan is late, Liam will reduce the payment by $5. Nathan begins his journey at 4:30 p.m.

How many miles should Nathan travel by boat to maximize his profit? Round to the nearest whole number

A gadget dealer purchases a smartwatch at a cost price that is 10% more than the cost price of a fitness band. He marks the price tag of the smartwatch at 20% above its cost price and the fitness band at 30% above its cost price. Later, he gives a discount of 25% on the smartwatch and 20% on the fitness band. If the difference between the selling prices of the smartwatch and the fitness band is Rs 500, what is the total marked price of 4 smartwatches and 5 fitness bands?

The policemen at three different places on the ground blow a whistle after every 42 sec, 60 sec, and 78 sec respectively. They all starts blowing the whistle simultaneously at 9:00:00 pm, when they blow whistle again together, a gang of thieves were spotted by them. They were at a distance of 150 meters from policemen 1, 180 meters from policemen 2 and 100 meters from policemen 3. When the policemen start the chase, the thieves splitted in three direction and starts running. The speed of the thief 1 is 10 m/sec and speed of policemen is 12.5 m/sec, the speed of the thief 2 is 8 m/sec and speed of policemen is 11 m/sec. The speed of the thief 3 is 9.5 m/sec and speed of policemen is 10 m/sec. 

If all three thieves run in the same direction at their average speed, and the time taken by the policemen to catch them is equal to the average of the individual times taken to catch each thief, at what time (approximate) will the thieves be caught, and what distance will they cover during this time interval?

A water reservoir is being filled using 4 high-capacity pumps and 10 standard pumps. Each high-capacity pump can fill water twice as fast as each standard pump. All pumps are switched on at the same time when the reservoir is empty.
When the reservoir was expected to be full, due to an undetected crack at the base, the reservoir was found to be only two-thirds full. The crack was then partially sealed, reducing the leakage by 50%.
If all pumps working together (without any leakage) can fill the reservoir in 7.5 hours, how much additional time will it take to completely fill the reservoir after the leak was half sealed?
What is the sum of all two-digit numbers that give a remainder of 5 when they are divided by 9?

Later, she added up all the numbers she had written and divided the total by what she believed was the correct count of numbers. Based on this, she calculated the average to be <inlineMath>43\frac{7}{{11}}</inlineMath>. Which number did Priyanshi mistakenly leave out of her list?

Two cargo ships, namely X and Y, start simultaneously from Port Alpha, sailing upstream towards Port Beta and reach there in 16.8 hours and 14 hours, respectively. A third cargo ship, Z, starts from Port Beta with the stream and reaches Port Alpha in 14 hours. Later, when ship Y starts from Port Beta with the stream, it takes 10.5 hours to reach Port Alpha.
Furthermore, when cargo ship Z starts from Port Alpha sailing upstream, after traveling for 10 hours, the crew spots a floating barrel drifting in the river. The ship Z continues to Port Beta, waits there for 6 hours, and then starts its return journey downstream towards Port Alpha. On the return trip, the ship encounters the same floating barrel at a distance of 112 km from the point where it was first spotted earlier. The ship Z takes 3 more hours to reach Port Alpha after this encounter.
Now, if ship Y and ship Z start simultaneously from Port Alpha and Port Beta, respectively, heading toward each other, then at what distance from Port Alpha will they meet?

  6. E, a doctor, is traveling, but not to Madrid or Vienna.
  7. D and I not travelling anywhere.
  8. B does not travel to Vienna or Rome

Which city is B traveling to?

Arjun, Karan, Nilesh, Tanmay, Sohail, Rohan, Deepak, Viren, and Manish are seated in two parallel rows, with six seats in each row. Only nine people are seated, meaning there are three vacant seats in total. Each person seated in a row faces someone from the opposite row or a vacant seat. Vacant seats do not face each other.
Each of them prefers a different car brand, namely: Ford, Toyota, Hyundai, Tata, Skoda, Mahindra, Kia, Maruti, and Honda. The people seated in Row-1 face south, while those in Row-2 face north. The information is not necessarily in the same order.
  1. The person sitting third to the right of Rohan is facing the person or vacant seat that is immediate right of the one who prefers Maruti.
  2. Nilesh is an immediate neighbor of vacant seats.
  3. Exactly one person sits between the ones who like Kia and Maruti.
  4. Rohan and the one who prefers Hyundai are facing each other.
  5. Sohail sits second to the right of the person who likes Tata.
  6. The people who like Toyota and Mahindra are immediate neighbors.
  7. Manish, who likes Skoda, is not adjacent to any vacant seat.

  11. Rohan's favorite car brand is Tata.
  12. The one who likes Ford sits third to the right of the one who likes Toyota.
  13. Viren likes neither Maruti nor Kia.
  14. Deepak sits immediately to the right of Nilesh, who does not face south.
Who among the following sits opposite to the person sitting second to the left of Sohail?

Faculty members in a business school can belong to one of four departments – Economics (ECO), Information Technology (IT), Marketing (MKT), and Operations (OPS).

The numbers of faculty members in ECO, IT, MKT, and OPS departments are 10, 8, 6, and 4 respectively. Prof. Anderson, Prof. Lee, Prof. Patel, and Prof. Williams are four candidates for the post of the Head of the School. Only one of the candidates is from the OPS department.

Every faculty member, including the four candidates, voted for the post. In each department, all faculty members who were not candidates voted for the same candidate. The rules for the election are as follows:

  • There cannot be more than two candidates from a single department.
  • A candidate cannot vote for himself/herself.
  • Faculty members cannot vote for a candidate from their own department.

After the election, the results were as follows:

  • Prof. Anderson received 4 votes.
  • Prof. Lee received 11 votes.
  • Prof. Patel received 6 votes.
  • Prof. Williams received 2 votes.

Prof. Anderson voted for Prof. Patel, Prof. Lee voted for Prof. Williams, Prof. Patel voted for Prof. Lee, and Prof. Williams voted for Prof. Anderson.

Which two candidates can belong to the same department?

In the mystical Kingdom of Eldora, the royal court is served by two types of advisors: Wisecallers, who always tell the truth, and Deceivers, who always lie. One day, four royal advisors — Lira, Galen, Mira, and Thorn — are summoned to discuss a matter of great importance. During the meeting, each makes a single statement:
  • Lira says, “Thorn and I belong to different groups.”
  • Galen says, “Mira is a Deceiver.”
  • Mira says, “Galen is a Deceiver.”
  • Thorn says, “At least two of us are Wisecallers.”
Determine how many of these royal advisors are Deceivers.

Eight family members, M, N, O, P, Q, R, S, and T, are seated around a rectangular table. One person sits at each corner, and two on each longer side. Those seated along the longer sides face the center, while those at the corners face outward. Each person has a different favorite sport: Cricket, Football, Tennis, Badminton, Hockey, Kabaddi, Wrestling, and Basketball. No sport is shared by more than one individual.
  • T’s sister enjoys Tennis and is seated second to the left of the one who likes Badminton.
  • R is not seated next to her sister-in-law, and she doesn't like Football.
  • P is T’s mother and is married to N, who is a fan of Basketball.
  • N is not seated next to any female member of the family.
  • T, who faces outward, is seated immediately to the left of M, who likes Hockey.
  • P is seated immediately to the left of Q, who is the only daughter of N.
  • S is seated at a corner, and likes Badminton.
  • S is the father of R, and R is married to T, who likes Wrestling.
  • O, the sister of P, is fond of Kabaddi.
  • M is the nephew of Q.

Who among the following is second to the left of the one whose favorite sport is Kabaddi?

options.text: The one whose favorite sport is Hockey
The one whose favorite sport is Football

questions.questionText:
A logistics company operates two regional hubs – Hub East and Hub West – for the distribution of goods. Each hub has three delivery zones, and the company tracks the number of parcels delivered per day and the average fuel cost per parcel (in ₹) for each zone. 
Data Set 1:Parcels Delivered Per Day

Data Set 2: Average Fuel Cost Per Parcel (in ₹)

The company plans to shift Zone B operations from Hub West to Hub East for one day due to a maintenance issue. If the total number of parcels delivered across both hubs remains the same, and the distribution capacity of Hub East increases proportionally across all its zones, what will be the total fuel cost incurred on that day for all deliveries?

  1. Motorbike (M1)
  2. Small Van (M2)
  3. Delivery Truck (M3)

questions.questionText:
A house was bought for Rs.8,00,000 and sold for Rs.9,00,000. After selling, the seller decided to reinvest the profit into buying a second property and took rest of the amount as a loan at a simple interest rate of 5% for 2 years. The second property was bought for Rs.6,00,000 and sold after 2 years for Rs.7,20,000.

What was the total percentage profit made by the seller from both transactions combined?

What percentage of the total selling price of both houses does the profit from the second house represent?

Mr. Sharma commutes daily from his home to his office, a fixed distance D. He has three modes of transport: Car, Bike, and Public Bus.
On Monday, he drives his car at 60 km/h for the first half of the distance and then at 80 km/h for the remaining half.
On Tuesday, he uses his bike. He travels at a constant speed for the first 30% of the distance. Due to heavy traffic, his speed decreases by 20% for the next 40% of the distance. For the final part of the journey, he increases his speed by 25% of his initial speed and covers the remaining distance. He takes a total of 2 hours on Tuesday.
On Wednesday, he takes the Public Bus. The bus travels at a certain speed for the first hour. It then stops for 15 minutes. After the stop, the driver, to make up for lost time, increases the speed by 10 km/h and covers the remaining 105 km in 1.5 hours. He observes that if the bus had not stopped, it would have reached the destination 30 minutes earlier.
  • What is the average speed of Mr. Sharma's commute on Monday?
  • If on Thursday, Mr. Sharma wants to reach his office in exactly 1 hour 45 minutes, at what uniform speed should he drive his car?

The first pie chart illustrates the revenue distribution from the National Book Fair 2022, which earned a total of Rs 250 crore. The second pie chart represents the revenue distribution from the National Book Fair 2023, which earned a total of Rs 500 crore.

Revenue distribution from the National Book Fair 2022
Revenue distribution from the National Book Fair 2023

If the revenue from Educational Games in Book Fair 2022 increases by 8% and the earnings from Music & Audiobooks decrease by 10%, how much more or less revenue would Book Fair 2022 generate compared to Book Fair 2023 in these specific segments?

Three partners, A, B, and C, invested in a business venture. They agreed to share the profits in the ratio 3: 5: 7. The durations for which each partner invested their capital were different. A invested for 6 months, B for 4 months, and C for 9 months. If the total profit earned was Rs. 28,000, how much profit did each partner receive, and what was the total investment made by each partner?

Study the following tables carefully and answer the questions that follow.

Data Set 1: Revenue (in ₹ crores) Generated from Five Products (A, B, C, D, E) Over Four Quarters of a Year

What is the total revenue generated by all the products in a year? The company decides to reinvest 60% of the annual profit into new product development. What is the total amount reinvested into new product development from all five products?

The main part of the house is a cube with side length 8 meters.
The roof is a triangular prism placed perfectly on top of the cube. The triangular face is an isosceles triangle with base 8 meters and height 3 meters, and the prism extends the full depth of the cube.

An international flight operates a route from Airport J to City K. The details of the flight are as follows:

Distance: 1,200 km

Cruising Speed: 800 km/hr

Climb and Descent Speed: 400 km/hr

Time Rules:

The flight departs Airport J at 3:00 pm.

The flight must ascend to cruising altitude, taking 30 minutes to climb at 400 km/hr.

The flight will cruise for 1 hour before encountering turbulence, which requires a descent to a lower altitude. The descent takes 20 minutes at 400 km/hr.

During the descent, the flight must also make an emergency stop for 15 minutes to address a mechanical issue.

After the descent, the flight resumes cruising for the remaining distance.

The flight also experiences a total delay of 45 minutes due to air traffic control.

Calculate the total travel time for the flight from Airport J to City K, including all phases of the flight (climb, cruise, descent, emergency stop, and delays). What is the expected arrival time at City K?

The telegraph and fax machine played major roles in revolutionising long-distance communication. The telegraph, developed in 19th century, was the first technology to allow instant messaging across great distances. Using Morse code, it enabled people to send information quickly through wires, changing how news, business, and government operations functioned. It reduced the delay of days or weeks in communication to just minutes. 

The fax machine, which became popular in the 20th century, allowed the transmission of scanned printed materials over telephone lines. This was especially useful in offices, as documents could be shared without physical delivery. Fax machines combined speed with the ability to send visual content like signatures, diagrams and hand-written notes.   

Which of the following best explains a cause-and-effect relationship from the passage?

options.text: The invention of the fax machine caused the disappearance of handwritten letters.
The need for faster communication led to the invention and use of the telegraph and fax, which greatly reduced delays in message delivery.
The popularity of email directly caused the creation of the telegraph.
The use of Morse code caused visual content to become more common in communication.

questions.questionText:
The global economy has undergone significant transformations over the past few decades, driven largely by the rise of globalisation, digital technologies and changing consumer behaviour. As economies become more interconnected, businesses have access to a global market, allowing for the exchange of goods, services and ideas across borders. However, the impact of globalisation has been uneven, with certain industries and countries benefiting more than others. The digital revolution, particularly the widespread adoption of the internet and mobile technology, has disrupted traditional business models, creating new opportunities for startups while also rendering some jobs obsolete. In this new landscape, companies are now tasked with navigating complex global supply chains, responding to shifting consumer demands and adapting to technological advancements. The future of the global economy hinges on its ability to foster inclusive growth, address inequality and manage the environmental impact of industrialisation.

Which of the following best captures the tone and overall summary of the passage?

options.text: The tone is overly pessimistic, and the passage focuses on the challenges of globalisation and the digital revolution, arguing that they have led to widespread economic decline and job loss.

The tone is critical yet balanced, and the passage examines the profound effects of globalisation and digital technologies on the global economy while stressing the need for inclusive growth and responsible environmental practices.

The tone is overly optimistic, and the passage highlights the positive outcomes of globalisation and digital technologies, suggesting that they have created economic prosperity and job opportunities worldwide.

The tone is harsh and dismissive, and the passage argues that globalisation and the digital revolution are temporary phenomena, with little long-term impact on the global economy or societal structures.

questions.questionText:
The Human Development Index (HDI) is a measure developed by the United Nations to assess the overall well-being and development of a country beyond mere economic growth. It combines three key dimensions: life expectancy (health), education (mean and expected years of schooling), and standard of living (gross national income per capita). By integrating these indicators, HDI aims to provide a more holistic picture of human progress, contrasting sharply with metrics like GDP, which focus solely on economic output.

While HDI offers valuable insights, it is not without limitations. It does not capture inequality within a country, nor does it reflect environmental sustainability, political freedom, or cultural richness. Two countries might have the same HDI but vastly different distributions of wealth or access to public services. As such, HDI serves as a useful starting point for evaluating development, but it must be supplemented with other indicators to gain a fuller understanding of societal well-being and quality of life.

Which of the following can be inferred from the passage about the use of HDI in measuring development?

options.text: While HDI improves upon traditional economic metrics, relying solely on it may obscure critical disparities and dimensions of well-being.
HDI eliminates the need for GDP or other indices since it already captures economic, social, and political conditions comprehensively.
Nations with identical HDI scores are guaranteed to have equitable resource distribution and high civic satisfaction.
HDI primarily focuses on a country’s political freedom and environmental stability, offering a complete picture of development.

questions.questionText:
I had always believed that lifestyles in the countryside had turned non-violent and predictable. That was till the night of the storm. The wind howled through the valley like a wounded beast, beating against the windows of my small cottage. I sat by the dim glow of a flickering candle, paying attention to the eerie creaks of the vintage timber floor. Then came the knock: sharp, deliberate, and oddly out of place in the chaos outdoors.

I hesitated. Who might be out in this weather? My heart pounded as I made my way to the door, my hands trembling as they gripped the handle. As I pulled it open, a shadowy figure stood before me, sopping wet and shivering. His eyes, darkish and pleading, met mine. ‘Please,’ he whispered, his voice slightly audible over the hurricane. ‘Help me.’

What is the predominant tone of the passage?

Folklore and poems have long served as vessels of cultural identity, but their role took on new dimensions during movements for national independence. In colonised nations like India, poets and folk artists began embedding subtle yet powerful nationalist messages in their art. These narratives, once rooted in myth and daily life, evolved into expressions of resistance against foreign rule. 

The accessibility of folk songs allowed even the illiterate masses to internalise ideas of unity, pride, and rebellion. Over time, such artistic expressions not only preserved indigenous traditions but also ignited collective consciousness and inspired political mobilisation. This transformation highlights the strategic use of culture as a tool for shaping identity and asserting autonomy in the face of oppression.

Which of the following best reflects the unintended yet transformative consequence of adapting cultural art forms during colonial resistance, as suggested by the passage?

options.text: They shifted from passive cultural artifacts to dynamic tools for social awakening, bridging literacy gaps and fostering political identity.
Their growing political tone led to a decline in aesthetic appreciation among traditionalists, altering their role in ceremonial life.
The infusion of nationalist themes caused regional variations in folklore to disappear, homogenising cultural expressions.
They became the sole mode of resistance available to oppressed communities, overshadowing other intellectual movements.

questions.questionText:
Electric current's magnetic effect is a basic idea that underpins many contemporary technological applications. A magnetic field surrounds a conductor when an electric current passes through it. The way that electricity and magnetism interact has transformed several industries, including transportation and healthcare. Electric motors, for instance, use this magnetic effect to generate mechanical motion that powers devices like electric cars, freezers, and fans. Transformers, which change the voltage in power transmission to enable long-distance electricity distribution without causing undue loss, require magnetic fields.

Strong magnetic fields are used by medical equipment like magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to provide finely detailed pictures of the human innards. As a result, medical diagnostics have greatly improved. Strong magnets are used to raise and move trains at extraordinarily high speeds with little friction, a technique known as magnetic levitation, or maglev. These uses demonstrate how electricity and magnetism can be combined to enhance productivity and creative uses in various industries.
 

Based on the passage, which of the following is the most accurate cause-and-effect relationship regarding the magnetic effect of electric current?

options.text: The flow of electric current causes a magnetic field, which leads to the creation of electric motors and transformers.
Electric motors and transformers generate magnetic fields, which then increase the flow of electric current.
The magnetic effect of electric current causes friction in trains, which slows them down.
Magnetic fields cause MRI machines to stop functioning, which disrupts medical diagnostics.

questions.questionText:
Mahadevi Verma, often hailed as the modern Meera of Hindi literature, was not only a poet but a philosopher, feminist, and visionary whose words defied the constraints of her time. As a leading figure of the Chhayavaad movement, she infused her poetry with mysticism and emotion, yet her true brilliance lay in her ability to interweave lyrical grace with profound philosophical depth. Her verses, delicate in form, were often a powerful response to patriarchal norms and spiritual confinement.

Her prose, though less discussed, demonstrated her command over social critique through subtle irony and sharp observation. In essays like Shrinkhala Ki Kadiyaan, she examined the layered oppression faced by women never through loud protest, but through quiet yet piercing introspection. She mastered the art of implication over declaration, allowing readers to arrive at truths rather than confronting them directly.

Mahadevi Verma’s contributions remain crucial not merely for their literary beauty but for their understated radicalism. She carved a voice for the feminine self in a literary world dominated by male narratives—not by shouting over them, but by writing around them with brilliance and restraint.

Which of the following best describes the author’s tone in the passage regarding Mahadevi Verma’s literary contributions?

options.text: Measured reverence with analytical depth, celebrating her legacy while acknowledging the intricacy of her method.
Mildly nostalgic and primarily descriptive, focusing on the literary context of the Chhayavaad era.
Detached and critical, evaluating her writings from a modern socio-political lens.
Assertively persuasive, urging the reader to accept Mahadevi Verma as the foremost literary feminist of her time.

questions.questionText:
In 1929, the stock market crash triggered a severe economic downturn known as the Great Depression. Businesses collapsed, unemployment soared and millions of people struggled to afford basic necessities. The widespread panic and loss of confidence in the financial system led to a sharp contraction in consumer spending and investment. As a result, the government implemented large-scale public works programmes and financial reforms to stabilise the economy. These measures aimed not only to revive economic activity but also to prevent future market collapses.
Select the primary cause and effect in the given scenario.

options.text:
Cause: The stock market crash of 1929
Effect: Millions of people struggled with basic living expenses.

Cause: High unemployment and financial struggles
Effect: The economy continued to deteriorate in the absence of any intervention.

Cause: Lack of business regulations
Effect: The stock market experienced rapid growth, and the economy stabilised.

Cause: Government intervention in the economy
Effect: The stock market crash deepened the economic losses, leading to further market collapses.

questions.questionText:
The transatlantic slave trade, which lasted from the 16th to the 19th century, forcibly transported millions of Africans to the Americas. While often condemned today for its brutal inhumanity, at the time, it was defended by many European powers as an economic necessity. Proponents argued that the trade fuelled the growth of industries such as sugar, cotton, and tobacco, creating wealth for empires and providing labour for expanding colonial economies. 

Opponents, however, viewed the practice as a moral atrocity, emphasising the dehumanisation, violence, and generational trauma it inflicted on African communities. Over time, abolitionist movements across Europe and the Americas challenged the economic justification, asserting that ethical responsibility must outweigh financial interests. The eventual dismantling of the trade reflected a growing recognition that no economic benefit could justify systemic human suffering. However, the legacy of the slave trade, visible in persistent racial inequalities and cultural dislocation, remains a deeply embedded part of global history.

Which option best demonstrates a nuanced understanding of both the supporting and opposing arguments surrounding the transatlantic slave trade as discussed in the passage?

options.text:
Supporting Argument: The slave trade was essential for industrial progress and should be considered a necessary historical phase.
Opposing Argument: Modern economies would have developed without slavery, rendering it historically irrelevant.

Supporting Argument: The trade was seen as economically advantageous by colonial powers due to the labour it supplied.
Opposing Argument: Abolitionists argued that ethical values should take precedence over financial profit.

Supporting Argument: European nations used the slave trade to civilise underdeveloped societies through forced labour.
Opposing Argument: The slave trade was ineffective in producing real economic growth for anyone involved.

Supporting Argument: The moral critique of slavery began only after it ended, proving it had long-lasting acceptance.
Opposing Argument: African societies benefited from their interactions with European traders.

questions.questionText: What can be inferred about the impact of different philosophical views on happiness regarding individual responsibility and external circumstances?

options.text: All philosophies agree that external circumstances are irrelevant to achieving happiness.
Stoicism and Buddhism both suggest happiness depends on inner control, while existentialism stresses personal choice despite external absurdity.
Existentialism denies the possibility of happiness, focusing solely on despair and meaninglessness.
Aristotle and Epicurus reject any connection between happiness and ethical living.

questions.questionText:
In today’s fast-paced world, multitasking is often praised as a valuable skill, especially among students and professionals trying to balance multiple responsibilities. However, cognitive research suggests that multitasking may not be as effective as commonly believed, particularly when it comes to learning and memory retention. Studies have shown that the human brain is not truly capable of focusing on multiple complex tasks at once. Instead, it rapidly switches attention from one task to another, resulting in divided focus and decreased efficiency.

When learners try to study while texting, watching videos, or browsing social media, their ability to process and retain information declines. This constant shifting of attention can lead to cognitive overload and shallow understanding. While it may feel productive, multitasking often results in longer completion times and more errors. Therefore, many educators and psychologists argue that focused, single-task learning is far more efficient and beneficial for deep comprehension and long-term retention. The belief in multitasking as a learning booster, they argue, may be more myth than reality.

Which of the following best summarises the central argument of the passage “Is Multitasking a Myth in Learning Efficiency?”

options.text: Multitasking is an essential skill in modern life, and students should be trained to handle multiple tasks at once for academic success.
While multitasking appears efficient, research shows it reduces learning effectiveness by dividing attention and overloading the brain.
The human brain can adapt to multitasking over time, making it a useful tool for learning and working in high-pressure environments.
Multitasking enhances memory and comprehension only when used alongside digital tools like videos and educational apps.

questions.questionText:
Indian politics has experienced significant transformation over the decades. In the early years post-independence, the political landscape was primarily dominated by the Indian National Congress, which played a central role in shaping the country's democratic foundations. However, over time, there has been a shift towards a multi-party system, with regional and smaller political parties gaining influence. This change has been particularly evident in the last few decades, as regional parties have increasingly secured power in various states, challenging the dominance of national parties. 

One of the key factors behind this shift has been the rise of identity-based politics, where issues like caste, religion, and language have been used to mobilise voters. As a result, coalition governments have become more common, leading to a more fragmented political environment. This has led to both positive and negative consequences, such as increased representation of diverse groups but also political instability and difficulty in policy implementation.

Based on the passage, which of the following best represents the cause-and-effect relationships discussed?

options.text: The dominance of national parties has led to increased political fragmentation and instability.
Political instability in India has resulted in the increased influence of smaller political parties.
The shift towards a multi-party system has resulted in a more centralised political environment.
The rise of identity-based politics has led to the formation of more coalition governments, which have caused political instability.

questions.questionText:
Cloud storage has already revolutionised the way individuals and organisations manage data, but its future promises even more transformative shifts. One key development lies in edge-integrated cloud storage, where data processing occurs closer to the source such as IoT devices minimising latency and bandwidth use. This approach is critical for real-time applications like autonomous vehicles and smart city infrastructure.

Simultaneously, AI-powered storage management is expected to evolve rapidly. Intelligent systems could automatically organise, optimise, and secure cloud data, predicting storage needs or identifying vulnerabilities before they become critical. Moreover, decentralised cloud storage, leveraging blockchain, may offer enhanced privacy and user control by distributing data across networks rather than relying on centralised data centres. 

Which of the following inferences can most reasonably be drawn from the passage regarding the direction of cloud storage evolution?

options.text: The future of cloud storage will prioritise minimising hardware dependence by eliminating edge devices and decentralising all processes.
Advancements in cloud storage are primarily aimed at increasing storage space rather than enhancing security, speed, or accessibility.
The integration of edge computing, AI, and decentralised systems reflects a broader trend toward making cloud storage more intelligent, efficient, and secure.
As cloud storage becomes more complex, it will require users to manually manage and secure their data without algorithmic assistance.

questions.questionText:
William Wordsworth, one of the central figures of English Romanticism, revolutionised poetry by turning away from the lavish language and rigid forms of the 18th century. Instead, he embraced simplicity, emotion, and nature as the heart of poetic expression. Born in 1770, Wordsworth’s deep connection with the natural world became the cornerstone of his poetic vision. He believed that nature was not only a source of beauty but also a moral and spiritual guide, capable of healing the human soul and awakening profound truths.
Wordsworth's collaboration with Samuel Taylor Coleridge on Lyrical Ballads in 1798 marked a defining moment in literary history. In this collection, he argued that poetry should reflect the language of ordinary people and the experiences of everyday life. His most famous works, such as Tintern Abbey and Ode on Intimations of Immortality, explore themes of memory, childhood, loss, and the sublime power of nature. His verses, infused with sincerity and reverence, continue to inspire generations with their quiet strength and philosophical depth.
Which of the following statements best supports the viewpoint expressed in the passage about William Wordsworth’s contribution to poetry?

options.text: Wordsworth’s emphasis on natural imagery and emotional depth made poetry more accessible and meaningful to the common reader.
Wordsworth’s rejection of traditional poetic forms weakened the structural beauty and discipline of classical poetry.
True poetry should maintain its complexity and elevated diction to distinguish it from everyday speech.
By simplifying language and focusing on nature, Wordsworth diminished poetry’s potential to explore deeper intellectual themes.

questions.questionText:
Terms or idioms used in scientific discourse to express responses, surprise, or highlight a particular observation or conclusion are known as scientific interjections. These interjections effectively highlight a point, demonstrate excitement, or sign a breakthrough in a scientific investigation. They are especially prevalent in written reports, talks, and presentations in various scientific domains, including biology, physics, chemistry, and engineering. 

For example, a biologist might recite Archimedes' well-known epiphany, ‘Eureka!’ when making a significant discovery. Likewise, expressions like ‘This is unexpected!’ or ‘What an interesting result!’ are frequently employed to emphasise the importance of an experimental result. 

In addition to bringing emotion and human expression to the frequently technical language of science, these interjections are crucial for conveying excitement and discovery, both of which are necessary for inspiring more research and investigation. Scientific interjections reflect the dynamic and constantly changing nature of scientific work in addition to making the process of scientific discovery more relatable.

 

Based on the passage, how do scientific interjections contribute to the scientific process beyond merely expressing emotions or reactions?

options.text: By generating excitement and fostering a deeper emotional connection with the discovery, encourages further inquiry.
By serving as a tool for clarifying the complex jargon commonly used in scientific studies.
By distracting the audience from the technical aspects of the discovery.
By replacing formal scientific language with simpler, more relatable expressions.

questions.questionText:
Tariffs, traditionally viewed as a means of economic protectionism, have increasingly become a double-edged sword in modern global trade. While they aim to support domestic industries by making foreign goods more expensive, the broader economic effects often raise critical concerns. Tariffs can lead to costlier raw materials and finished products, indirectly burdening domestic producers and consumers alike. 
In highly interconnected global markets, such measures may distort supply chains, provoke retaliatory tariffs, and reduce overall trade efficiency. Policymakers must therefore weigh immediate political or economic gains against the long-term risks of reduced competitiveness and strained international ties. Tariffs may serve strategic purposes, but are rarely without economic trade-offs.
What higher-order conclusion can be drawn from the passage about the use of tariffs in a globally interconnected economy?

options.text: Tariffs, though politically expedient, can introduce hidden inefficiencies that outweigh their intended benefits in open-market economies.
The imposition of tariffs is primarily a symbolic gesture, lacking measurable impact in interconnected trade networks.
Long-term national prosperity is best secured through sustained tariff regimes that prioritise domestic production over global collaboration.
Tariff policies serve as neutral tools that affect all economies symmetrically, regardless of their size or integration level.

questions.questionText:
Statements:

  1. The Nalanda University, established in the 5th century CE in India, become one of the first international residential universities, attracting students from as far away as China, Korea, and Persia.
  2. It housed an in-depth library, ‘Dharma Gunj’ or ‘Mountain of Knowledge,’ said to have held hundreds of manuscripts on topics starting from Buddhism and philosophy to medication, arithmetic, and astronomy.
  3. When it was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in the 12th century, it reportedly burned for months, symbolising no longer simply the loss of books however the disintegration of a highbrow technology.
  4. Some argue that the destruction of Nalanda marked a turning point that hindered scientific progress near the location for centuries, at the same time as others contend that India’s knowledge systems continued to thrive in unique bureaucracy.

Which of the following arguments supports the idea that Nalanda’s destruction hindered scientific progress?

options.text: The university’s loss erased a vast repository of scientific knowledge, setting back research and innovation for generations.
India’s intellectual traditions adapted and evolved, continuing to flourish through regional schools like those in Kerala and Jaipur.
The destruction of Nalanda was primarily a symbolic event, with little impact on the broader trajectory of knowledge.
Knowledge from Nalanda had already spread across Asia, ensuring that its teachings lived on elsewhere.

questions.questionText:
The suffrage movement was a pivotal chapter in the struggle for gender equality, and women played a central role in driving it forward. Leaders like Susan B. Anthony, Emmeline Pankhurst, and Sarojini Naidu used public speaking, petitions, and peaceful protests to demand voting rights for women. These efforts were not limited to one country; women across the world organised marches, wrote letters, and formed groups to push for political inclusion. Many supporters argued that giving women the right to vote was a matter of justice and would lead to more balanced and inclusive governance. 

On the other hand, some opponents believed that women's involvement in politics would disrupt traditional social roles or distract from family duties. Despite such resistance, the determination of suffragists helped bring about significant legal changes, ultimately expanding democratic rights and setting the stage for future gender reforms.


Which of the following best reflects a balanced evaluation of both the supporting and opposing perspectives on women's participation in the suffrage movement, as discussed in the passage?

options.text: Advocates viewed suffrage as a path to equity and reform, while critics feared it would challenge deeply rooted societal structures.
Suffragists believed in the superiority of female leadership, whereas opponents doubted women’s intellectual abilities.
Supporters wanted women to replace men in politics, but traditionalists demanded complete political exclusion.
Campaigners prioritised individual rights, while detractors emphasised the need for women to focus on education over activism.

questions.questionText:
Imagine a time when human beings had to drag heavy masses through rough ground, straining each muscle. Life was hard and exhausting, till a person, somewhere, had an idea that modified the entirety of technology: the wheel. Around 3500 BCE, this amazing invention set humanity on a path to unstoppable progress. What commenced as a timber disk soon converted into carts, wagons, and later, complicated equipment. 

The wheel didn’t just make existence simpler; it powered civilisations, connected humans, and shaped the modern-day world. It’s exceptional to think how one humble concept, born from necessity, keeps turning even nowadays, moving us forward in more approaches than one.

Based on the passage, which statement best describes the tone of the passage?

options.text: The passage celebrates the wheel’s invention as a remarkable achievement that continues to impact humanity.
The passage criticises the wheel’s invention, suggesting it created more problems than it solved.
The passage focuses on the struggles of early humans and how life remained difficult despite the wheel’s invention.
The passage explains the wheel’s invention in a purely factual and neutral manner.

questions.questionText:
In a formal company, communication plays a critical role in making sure that goals are met efficiently and constantly. The sorts of communication normally fall into three classes: downward, upward, and horizontal. Downward communication involves messages from higher to lower level within the hierarchy, such as instructions, feedback, and policies ensuring that the strategic vision is implemented operationally. Upward communication, lets in subordinates to share reports, demanding situations, and recommendations with their superiors, fostering transparency and responsiveness. 
Horizontal communication occurs among peers or departments at the same level, important for coordination and collaboration across capabilities. Increasingly, formal organizations are incorporating digital platforms to facilitate all three sorts, allowing asynchronous but traceable exchanges. However, demanding situations remain in preserving clarity, handling quantity, and heading off misinterpretation mainly in highly based environments. 
Which of the following best reflects the author’s underlying concern about communication in formal organizations?

options.text: Digital communication tools are replacing traditional forms of communication entirely in organizations.
While structured communication types support organizational functioning, modern tools introduce new challenges in ensuring effectiveness.
Upward communication is inherently less valued in formal settings, leading to decision-making delays.
Horizontal communication leads to informal alliances that weaken the formal structure of organizations.
